skill.name: responsive-design
skill.description: Create responsive web designs for phones, tablets, desktops, and large screens using mobile-first layout patterns.
skill.summary: Guide mobile-first responsive layouts with CSS Grid, Flexbox, media queries, container queries, and responsive images.
skill.author: supercent-io

security_audit.summary: All static findings were false positives caused by Markdown code fences, CSS examples, reference links, and related-skill documentation links. No prompt injection, malware intent, credential access, data exfiltration, runtime command execution, or filesystem access was found in SKILL.md or SKILL.toon.

remediation.suggestion: Keep code examples fenced with explicit language labels and avoid standalone shell-like backtick patterns where possible.
Use marketplace skill identifiers or non-relative documentation links to avoid path-traversal false positives.

remediation.issue: External reference links are present in the skill document.
remediation.suggestion: Label links as documentation references and avoid instructing agents to fetch external pages automatically.

static_findings.snippet: 2. **Duplicate code**: Avoid repeating same styles across all breakpoints
2. **Flexbox vs Grid**: Flexbox for 1-dimensional, Grid for 2-dimensional

content.value_statement: Fixed layouts fail on phones, tablets, and wide screens. This skill guides mobile-first CSS, breakpoints, images, and layout patterns.
actual_capabilities: Plans mobile-first layouts that scale from small screens to large desktops.
Explains when to use CSS Grid, Flexbox, media queries, and container queries.
Provides responsive image patterns using srcset, sizes, picture, and CSS image sets.
Defines practical breakpoint ranges and reusable CSS custom properties.
Shows navigation and product grid examples for common frontend screens.
limitations: Does not run browser tests or verify layouts in real devices by itself.
Does not generate a complete design system or visual brand guide.
Examples are generic and need adaptation to each application framework.
Accessibility guidance is limited and should be paired with an accessibility review.

use_cases.title: Launch a Mobile-First Page
use_cases.description: Create a layout that starts with a phone view and expands cleanly for tablet and desktop screens.

use_cases.title: Modernize a Fixed Layout
use_cases.description: Replace fixed widths with flexible grids, relative spacing, and breakpoint-based adjustments.

use_cases.title: Prepare Responsive UI Requirements
use_cases.description: Document breakpoint behavior, image handling, and layout expectations for a new web interface.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Responsive Layout
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new page layout.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the responsive-design skill to create a mobile-first layout for a simple landing page with header, content, and footer sections.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Fixed CSS
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for improving an existing page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the responsive-design skill to convert this fixed-width layout into a mobile-first responsive layout with clear breakpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Design Responsive Cards
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for reusable product or content cards.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the responsive-design skill to design a card grid that changes from one column on mobile to four columns on large screens.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Responsive Behavior
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for reviewing a full interface.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the responsive-design skill to audit this interface for layout overflow, breakpoint duplication, image scaling, and typography issues.

output_examples.input: A product listing page needs to work on mobile, tablet, desktop, and large screens.
output_examples.output: A mobile-first grid plan with one, two, three, and four column states, plus spacing and image sizing guidance.

output_examples.input: A desktop navigation bar needs a mobile menu.
output_examples.output: A responsive navigation approach with a mobile toggle, accessible state labels, and horizontal links on wider screens.

output_examples.input: A legacy page uses fixed widths and large images.
output_examples.output: A refactor checklist covering max-width containers, relative units, responsive images, and viewport testing steps.

best_practices: Start with the smallest supported screen and add complexity at wider breakpoints.
Use Grid for two-dimensional layouts and Flexbox for one-dimensional alignment.
Test real content at each breakpoint before finalizing spacing and image behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on fixed page widths for primary layout containers.
Do not duplicate the same styles across every breakpoint.
Do not treat responsive images as optional when page performance matters.

faq.question: Does this skill write production CSS?
faq.answer: It provides production-oriented patterns and examples, but final code should match your project conventions.

faq.question: Can it help with existing layouts?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide conversion from fixed desktop layouts to flexible mobile-first layouts.

faq.question: Does it support CSS Grid and Flexbox?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when each layout method is useful and includes examples for both.

faq.question: Does it include responsive image guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers srcset, sizes, picture elements, CSS backgrounds, and image-set usage.

faq.question: Does it replace accessibility testing?
faq.answer: No. It mentions related accessibility concerns, but it does not perform a full accessibility audit.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
